title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
gist: A conference preview of QCon AI New York (Dec 15-16, 2026) framing production AI pain points: agent identity and authorization, eval trust, LLM context cost, and review bottlenecks from AI-generated code. It cites scale figures from LinkedIn's Kubernetes ops agent and AI code review system.

insights.claim: Teams giving agents production access today face a bad choice between long-lived service accounts and access scoped too narrowly for the agent to finish its task, motivating new identity and authorization models for agents.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent identity and authorization is an emerging infrastructure and security product category.
insights.locator: The QCon AI opening keynote describes two bad options

insights.claim: LinkedIn's Kubernetes ops agent works across more than 500,000 nodes and 5 million pods, with server-side guardrails such as rate limits and peer approval for production changes.
insights.speaker: Ronak Nathani (session description)
insights.so_what: Shows agents already operating at hyperscale infrastructure with human-approval controls.
insights.locator: See what those controls look like on a live platform

insights.claim: DoorDash's agentic ordering team argues engineers should apply one judge to both simulated and production sessions so improvements measured before launch carry into production.
insights.speaker: Fabio Flores (session description)
insights.so_what: Unified evals are key to trusting agent releases and avoiding regressions.
insights.locator: An eval is useful when engineers trust the score

insights.claim: Agent prototypes can become too expensive in production as context grows, and prompt compression and ordering that increase provider cache hits, plus tiered storage for conversation history, are cost levers.
insights.speaker: Tejas Chopra (session description)
insights.so_what: LLM inference cost control is shifting to context engineering, affecting token spend.
insights.locator: Agent workloads that worked as prototypes

insights.claim: As AI tools generate more code, human review becomes the bottleneck, and LinkedIn filters low-confidence AI review findings before developers see them across tens of thousands of pull requests a week in about 10,000 repositories.
insights.speaker: Min Chen (session description)
insights.so_what: The value shifts from code generation to review and verification tooling.

insights.claim: Google Cloud's DORA lead argues AI amplifies what an organization already does well and badly, so AI maturity should be assessed beyond adoption metrics, identifying which existing problems AI will worsen.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey (session description)
insights.so_what: AI productivity gains are uneven; firms with weak engineering practices may see worse outcomes.
insights.locator: Faster output does not help every organization equally

insights.claim: The conference markets itself as vendor-neutral, practitioner-led sessions with a ratio of one speaker per eleven attendees, aiming to deliver patterns and failure lessons for senior engineers deciding on production AI.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Promotional; indicates demand for production-AI hindsight rather than prototypes.
